name: name##_SPLAY_INSERT
prose: Generated function name_SPLAY_INSERT(head, elm), defined by SPLAY_GENERATE. If the tree is empty, elm's left and right links are set to NULL, elm becomes the root and NULL is returned. Otherwise it first splays the tree around elm (name_SPLAY, which rearranges the tree), compares elm with the new root and: if elm sorts before the root, elm takes the root's left subtree as its left child and the old root as its right child (the root's left link is cleared); if elm sorts after the root, elm takes the root's right subtree as its right child and the old root as its left child (the root's right link is cleared); in both cases elm becomes the root and NULL is returned. If a node with an equal key is the root after splaying, that existing node is returned and elm is not linked in, although the tree has been splayed. cmp is the user-supplied comparison.
note: sys/tree.h; added that the tree is restructured even when a duplicate is found (tree.h:173-196)

name: name##_SPLAY_REMOVE
prose: Generated function name_SPLAY_REMOVE(head, elm), defined by SPLAY_GENERATE. If the tree is empty it returns NULL. Otherwise it splays the tree around elm and, if the root now compares equal to elm, removes that root: when the root has no left child, its right child becomes the root; otherwise the left subtree becomes the tree, is splayed again around elm so its largest node is the root, and the old right subtree is attached as that root's right child. In that case it returns elm, the argument pointer, not necessarily the node that was unlinked (they compare equal but may be different objects). If no node compares equal it returns NULL and the tree has only been splayed.
note: sys/tree.h; prior prose said the unlinked node is returned; code returns elm (tree.h:214)

name: name##_SPLAY
prose: Generated function name_SPLAY(head, elm), defined by SPLAY_GENERATE; it returns void. It performs a top-down splay: the tree must be non-empty (head->sph_root is passed to the comparison without a NULL check), and afterwards the root is the node whose key equals elm's key if there is one, otherwise the last node on the search path (the node closest to the key), with the tree restructured by rotations and left/right link splicing but containing the same nodes and still ordered by cmp.
note: sys/tree.h; added non-empty precondition: cmp(elm, head->sph_root) at tree.h:228 dereferences the root

name: name##_SPLAY_MINMAX
prose: Generated function name_SPLAY_MINMAX(head, __comp), defined by SPLAY_GENERATE; it returns void. The tree must be non-empty and __comp must be non-zero: with __comp < 0 it splays the minimum node to the root and with __comp > 0 the maximum node; with __comp == 0 neither branch of the loop body breaks out, so it would not terminate. The set of nodes in the tree is unchanged.
note: sys/tree.h; tree.h:257-288

name: name##_SPLAY_FIND
prose: Generated function name_SPLAY_FIND(head, elm), a static inline function defined by SPLAY_PROTOTYPE. If the tree is empty it returns NULL without changes. Otherwise it splays the tree around elm (so the tree is restructured even on a miss) and returns the root if cmp(elm, root) == 0, or NULL otherwise.
note: sys/tree.h; tree.h:138-147

name: name##_SPLAY_NEXT
prose: Generated function name_SPLAY_NEXT(head, elm), a static inline function defined by SPLAY_PROTOTYPE. It splays the tree around elm (the tree must be non-empty), then returns the leftmost node of elm's right subtree, or NULL if elm has no right child. It reads the right child of elm itself (not of the root), so the result is the in-order successor only when elm was found and has become the root, i.e. when elm is in the tree.
note: sys/tree.h; tree.h:149-161; non-empty precondition added

name: name##_SPLAY_MIN_MAX
prose: Generated function name_SPLAY_MIN_MAX(head, val), a static inline function defined by SPLAY_PROTOTYPE. It calls name_SPLAY_MINMAX(head, val) and returns the root: the minimum node for val < 0 and the maximum node for val > 0. The tree must be non-empty and val must be non-zero (the macros SPLAY_MIN and SPLAY_MAX test for an empty tree first and pass SPLAY_NEGINF or SPLAY_INF).

name: name##_RB_INSERT_COLOR
prose: Generated function name_RB_INSERT_COLOR(head, parent, elm), defined by RB_GENERATE_INSERT_COLOR; it restores the rank-balance of a rank-balanced tree after elm was linked as a new leaf child of parent. It walks upward from parent while the rank of the subtree grew: if the edge from parent to elm was long it is shortened and the function returns NULL; if both edges of parent become short it continues one level up; otherwise it performs one or two rotations (RB_ROTATE, then RB_SWAP_CHILD to reattach the rotated subtree to its grandparent or the head), updates augmentation with RB_AUGMENT_CHECK for the elements rotated down, and returns the element 'child' that became the root of the rotated subtree. It returns NULL when no rotation was needed, including when the loop reaches the root. The caller keeps ownership of all nodes and no memory is allocated.
note: slice cut the head; real definition is RB_GENERATE_INSERT_COLOR in tree.h:524-625; return paths at 550, 622, 624

name: sysctl_ffs_fsck
prose: sysctl_ffs_fsck(SYSCTL_HANDLER_ARGS) is the write-only sysctl handler through which fsck_ffs submits filesystem repair commands; the slice shows only the later cases of its switch. It returns EBADRPC if the request has no new value or newlen exceeds sizeof(struct fsck_cmd), the error from SYSCTL_IN, ERPCMISMATCH if cmd.version is not FFS_CMD_VERSION, the error from getvnode on cmd.handle with CAP_FSCK, EINVAL if the file is not a regular file or directory (dropping the file reference) or is not on a 'ufs' mount (also ending the write started with vn_start_write), and EROFS if the mount is read-only. Otherwise it holds a write reference on the mount (vn_start_write) and dispatches on the sysctl OID number: FFS_SET_FLAGS sets or clears fs_flags bits; FFS_ADJ_REFCNT, FFS_ADJ_BLKCNT, FFS_ADJ_DEPTH (ENOTDIR for non-directories) and FFS_SET_SIZE look up an inode by number (ffs_vget) and adjust its link count, block count, directory depth or size, then call ffs_update; FFS_DIR_FREE and FFS_FILE_FREE free a range of inodes with ffs_freefile, stopping at the first error; FFS_BLK_FREE frees a range of blocks with ffs_blkfree; FFS_ADJ_NDIR, NBFREE, NIFREE, NFFREE and NUMCLUSTERS add cmd.value to the matching superblock summary counter; FFS_SET_CWD changes the caller's current directory to the inode (change_dir); FFS_SET_DOTDOT rewrites '..' in the current directory with ufs_dirrewrite; FFS_UNLINK drops the mount write reference first (setting mp to NULL) and calls kern_funlinkat; any other OID gives EINVAL. After the switch the file reference is dropped with fdrop and the write reference is finished (a no-op for mp == NULL), and the case's error is returned.
note: slice cut the head; real function sysctl_ffs_fsck (ffs_alloc.c:3279-3620), read in full; old prose 'with fp dropped ... on every path' is true after the early checks (3306-3321 drop fp and the write in their own way)

name: softdep_flushfiles
prose: softdep_flushfiles(oldmnt, flags, td) flushes all vnodes and soft-dependency worklist items of the mount; oldmnt must be a soft-updates mount. It starts with loopcnt = 10 and retry_flush_count = 3. In each loop iteration it calls ffs_flushfiles(oldmnt, flags | early, td), where early is EARLYFLUSH when MNTK_UNMOUNT is set in the mount and retry_flush_count != 1 (this applies to the initial attempt as well as the first retry), otherwise 0, and then softdep_flushworklist(oldmnt, &depcount, td); the loop ends on an error from either call or when depcount is 0. If the loop ran out (loopcnt reached 0) it panics when MNTK_UNMOUNT is set and otherwise sets EBUSY. If there is no error so far it calls softdep_waitidle and keeps its result. If still no error and the mount is being unmounted, it checks for remaining work (vnodes on the mount's list, or quota vnodes under QUOTA): if there is, it decrements retry_flush_count and, while that is still positive, resets loopcnt to 3 and repeats from the start; when retry_flush_count reaches 0 it sets EBUSY instead. It returns 0 or the first error (EBUSY, or an error from ffs_flushfiles, softdep_flushworklist or softdep_waitidle).
note: reviewer round15 right: early = EARLYFLUSH on the initial unmount attempt too (ffs_softdep.c:2123-2124: ((retry_flush_count == 1 || !unmount) ? 0 : EARLYFLUSH)); slice contains the second (real) definition at ffs_softdep.c:2093

name: ffs_mount
prose: ffs_mount(mp) mounts or updates a UFS/FFS filesystem. It returns EINVAL if vfs_filteropt rejects the option list; it creates the FFS inode and dinode UMA zones on first use; deletes the groupquota and userquota options; gets the 'from' option with vfs_getopts and returns that error if it fails (ENOENT when absent); sets MNT_UNTRUSTED, MNT_ACLS, MNT_SNAPSHOT (removing 'snapshot' from the option lists) and MNT_NFS4ACLS from the options, returning EINVAL if both acls and nfsv4acls are given; then clears MNTK_FPLOOKUP and ORs the new flags into mnt_flag. For a snapshot request it returns EINVAL if MNT_UPDATE is not set, and otherwise returns ffs_snapshot(mp, fspec) directly (so a successful snapshot returns 0 before vfs_mountedfrom and before MNTK_FPLOOKUP is set). Otherwise it drops the busy reference for an update, looks up fspec with namei, re-takes the busy reference, and returns the error from namei, from vn_isdisk_error (not a disk) or from the permission check VOP_ACCESS followed by priv_check(PRIV_VFS_MOUNT_PERM), releasing the device vnode on those paths. For a new mount it calls ffs_mountfs and returns its error (releasing the vnode). For an update it returns EINVAL if the named device differs from the mounted one; if the filesystem is writable and 'ro' was requested it suspends writes, flushes files (softdep_flushfiles or ffs_flushfiles), updates the superblock and marks the mount read-only, returning the error and restoring read-write state (and MNT_SOFTDEP) if the flush or ffs_sbupdate fails, or the error of vn_start_write / vfs_write_suspend_umnt; it runs ffs_reload when MNT_RELOAD is set, returning its error; and for a read-only filesystem asked to become writable it checks VOP_ACCESS/priv_check on the original device, returns EPERM if the filesystem is unclean and neither forced nor an allowed soft-updates case, requests write access with g_access, suspends writes, clears read-only, starts soft updates (softdep_mount) and writes the superblock with ffs_sbupdate, restoring the read-only state and returning the error if softdep_mount or ffs_sbupdate fails, and resumes writes. Finally, on success of the new-mount or update path it clears MNT_ASYNC when soft updates is mounted, keeps MNT_ACLS / MNT_NFS4ACLS from the superblock flags, sets MNTK_FPLOOKUP unless MNT_ACLS, MNT_NFS4ACLS or MNT_UNION is set (panicking if it was already set), calls vfs_mountedfrom and returns 0.
note: reviewer round15 right: snapshot success returns before vfs_mountedfrom/MNTK_FPLOOKUP (ffs_vfsops.c:420-424); round2 prose already says ENOENT/vfs_getopts error; original review right that flushing only happens on the rw to ro transition; function at ffs_vfsops.c:348-719

name: QCMD

name: ufs_setattr
prose: ufs_setattr(ap) is the VOP_SETATTR implementation for UFS: ap->a_vp is the vnode, ap->a_vap the requested attributes (fields not to change are VNOVAL) and ap->a_cred the credential. Checks and changes happen in this order, each returning the stated value: EINVAL if va_type is not VNON, or any of va_nlink, va_fsid, va_fileid, va_blocksize, va_rdev, (int)va_bytes or va_gen is not VNOVAL. If va_flags is set: EOPNOTSUPP for unsupported flag bits; EROFS on a read-only mount; the error from VOP_ACCESS(VADMIN); for a caller with PRIV_VFS_SYSFLAGS, the securelevel_gt error if system flags are currently set and EPERM if the snapshot flag would be toggled; for a caller without it, EPERM if any of SF_NOUNLINK, SF_IMMUTABLE or SF_APPEND is currently set or any settable system flag would change; otherwise the flags are stored, IN_CHANGE is set and UFS_UPDATE is called; if the new flags include IMMUTABLE or APPEND the function returns right away with the UFS_UPDATE result (0 or its error), skipping every other requested attribute, otherwise the UFS_UPDATE result is not used. Then, if the inode has IMMUTABLE or APPEND set, it returns EPERM whether or not other attributes were requested. Owner or group change: EROFS on read-only mounts, else the error from ufs_chown. If va_size is set: EISDIR for a directory; for VLNK and VREG, EROFS on a read-only mount, EPERM for a snapshot, then the errors of vn_rlimit_trunc or UFS_TRUNCATE; for any other file type the function returns 0 at once and ignores the size and every later change (times, mode). If any of atime, mtime or birthtime is set: EROFS on read-only mounts, EPERM for a snapshot, the error from vn_utimes_perm, then the times are stored (birthtime only on UFS2) and UFS_UPDATE is called, returning its error. If va_mode is set: EROFS on read-only mounts, EPERM if a snapshot would get write or execute bits, otherwise the result of ufs_chmod. If no attribute is requested (and the inode is not immutable/append-only) it returns 0.
note: reviewers right: original (size ignored for unsupported types, birthtime UFS2 only), round2 (EISDIR), round15 (early return after flags when IMMUTABLE/APPEND). Prior prose also wrong that va_type must be VNOVAL (it must be VNON) and that EPERM for immutable needs further attributes requested (ufs_vnops.c:717-718 returns EPERM unconditionally)

name: ufs_chmod
prose: ufs_chmod(vp, mode, cred, td) changes the permission bits of the inode of vp; the inode must be locked by the caller and stays locked. It returns the error from VOP_ACCESSX(vp, VWRITE_ACL, ...) if that fails; EFTYPE if vp is not a directory, mode has the sticky bit and priv_check_cred(PRIV_VFS_STICKYFILE) fails; the priv_check_cred(PRIV_VFS_SETGID) error if mode has setgid and the caller is not a member of the inode's group; and the priv_check_cred(PRIV_VFS_ADMIN) error if mode has setuid and the inode's owner is not cred->cr_uid. Otherwise it replaces the ALLPERMS bits of i_mode with those of mode, updates the on-disk copy and sets IN_CHANGE. When UFS_ACL is compiled in and the mount has MNT_NFS4ACLS, it then resynchronises the NFS4 ACL from the new mode (ufs_update_nfs4_acl_after_mode_change) and an error from that is returned without calling UFS_UPDATE; if no error and IN_CHANGE is set it returns the result of UFS_UPDATE(vp, 0), otherwise 0.
note: prose checked against ufs_vnops.c:872-921; the mode change is applied before the ACL resync / UFS_UPDATE and is not undone on their errors

name: redzone_size_ntor
prose: redzone_size_ntor(nsize) returns the size of the allocation that must be made to hold nsize bytes plus the red zones: nsize + redzone_roundup(nsize) + REDZONE_FSIZE (16). redzone_roundup(n) first raises n to at least REDZONE_HSIZE (the size of a stack record, an unsigned long and 16 bytes), then returns 128, 256, 512, 1024 or 2048 for the first of those that is at least n, and PAGE_SIZE for anything larger (so for n above PAGE_SIZE it still returns PAGE_SIZE). Thus the result is between nsize + 144 and nsize + PAGE_SIZE + 16. The arithmetic is on u_long and wraps when nsize is within PAGE_SIZE + 16 of ULONG_MAX. The function has no side effects.
note: reviewer round15 right: redzone_roundup returns PAGE_SIZE even when n > PAGE_SIZE (redzone.c:55-72), so the 'at least max(nsize, HSIZE)' claim was wrong; round2 right about the overflow bound

name: swap_reserve
prose: swap_reserve(incr) returns swap_reserve_by_cred(incr, curthread->td_ucred), with incr a byte count that must be a multiple of PAGE_SIZE (KASSERT in the callee). swap_reserve_by_cred first, when RACCT is enabled, charges RACCT_SWAP to curproc under the process lock and returns false at once if racct_add fails. It then atomically adds atop(incr) pages to swap_reserved; computes the limit from swap_total, adding free non-wired memory when SWAP_RESERVE_ALLOW_NONWIRED is set in vm_overcommit and the new total exceeds swap_total; if SWAP_RESERVE_FORCE_ON is set, the new total exceeds the limit and priv_check(PRIV_VM_SWAP_NOQUOTA) fails, it takes the failure path. Otherwise it calls swap_reserve_by_cred_rlimit, which adds the pages to the user's ui_vmsize and, only when SWAP_RESERVE_RLIMIT_ON is set, the result exceeds RLIMIT_SWAP and priv_check(PRIV_VM_SWAP_NORLIMIT) fails, undoes that addition and reports failure; on such a failure the swap_reserved increment is also undone. It returns true on success. On either failure it prints a rate-limited message naming the uid and pid, undoes the RACCT charge when RACCT is enabled, and returns false. The racct failure path returns false without a message and with no counters changed.
note: prose from earlier round checked against swap_pager.c:258-330; round 2 reviewer right that FORCE_ON is required for the overcommit failure; the function itself only forwards to swap_reserve_by_cred

name: vm_domainset_iter_page
prose: vm_domainset_iter_page(di, obj, domain, pages) advances a page-allocation domain iterator after a failed allocation. In NUMA kernels, if vm_domainset_iter_next finds another domain it stores it in *domain and returns 0. Otherwise, if neither VM_ALLOC_WAITOK nor VM_ALLOC_WAITFAIL is set in di->di_flags it returns ENOMEM. Otherwise, if obj is non-NULL it unlocks the object write lock and, only if pages is also non-NULL, resets the pctrie iterator; it waits with vm_wait_doms(&di->di_valid_mask, 0); it then re-locks obj if non-NULL; then it returns ENOMEM if VM_ALLOC_WAITFAIL is set, and otherwise restarts the search with vm_domainset_iter_first, returning 0 if a domain was found (stored in *domain) and ENOMEM if not. In a kernel without NUMA the function does nothing and returns EJUSTRETURN. obj, if non-NULL, must be write-locked on entry and is locked again on every return path.
note: reviewers right: round2 (obj re-locked after vm_wait_doms) and round15 (pages reset only when obj != NULL, vm_domainset.c:292-296); original right about the non-NUMA EJUSTRETURN (365-371)

name: vm_ksubmap_init
prose: vm_ksubmap_init(kmi) sizes and creates boot-time kernel memory structures and returns void. It makes two passes over kern_vfs_bio_buffer_alloc(v, physmem_est), where physmem_est is physmem limited to the size of kernel_map in pages: the first pass computes the required size, then memory is allocated (with kmem_alloc_attr below 4 GB when VM_FREELIST_DMA32 is defined, falling back to kmem_malloc(M_ZERO | M_WAITOK)), and the second pass assigns addresses; it panics if no memory could be obtained or if the two passes disagree on the size. It allocates the clean map with kva_alloc for nbuf * BKVASIZE + bio_transient_maxcnt * maxphys bytes and records clean_sva/clean_eva, sets kmi->buffer_sva and buffer_eva and initialises the buffer arena with vmem_init (with a quantum cache when mp_ncpus > 4); if bio_transient_maxcnt is non-zero it initialises transient_arena right after the buffer arena with size bio_transient_maxcnt * maxphys. Finally it computes the exec map size from exec_map_entries (8 * mp_ncpus on LP64, 2 * mp_ncpus + 4 otherwise), exec_map_entry_size = round_page(PATH_MAX + ARG_MAX), the tunable vm.exec_map_guard_pages (default 1) and 64 extra pages, and creates exec_map and pipe_map (size maxpipekva) as submaps of kernel_map with kmem_subinit.
note: slice cut the head (vm_init.c:175-286); old prose claimed 'always returns normally' but the function can panic at 227 and 235, and kmi->buffer_eva is set by this function rather than being a precondition

name: vm_map_entry_pred
prose: Static inline function vm_map_entry_pred(entry) returns the in-order predecessor of entry in the vm_map entry tree (a threaded splay tree in which an empty left link points to the predecessor). It sets prior = entry->left; if prior->right->start is less than entry->start it follows prior = prior->right until prior->right == entry, and then returns prior; otherwise (prior->right->start >= entry->start) it returns entry->left itself. entry, entry->left and entry->left->right must be valid non-NULL pointers. It reads the tree only and takes no locks.
note: slice cut the head; vm_map.c:1033-1044. Reviewer round15 right: the returned node is entry->left when prior->right->start >= entry->start, not always the node whose right pointer is entry

name: vm_phys_early_alloc
prose: vm_phys_early_alloc(domain, alloc_size) takes physical memory out of phys_avail[] before the page allocator is running and returns its physical address (it never returns an error). domain must be -1 or a valid domain (checked by KASSERT only). On NUMA kernels with a non-NULL mem_affinity it scans the array up to the first entry of zero size (end == start), picks the largest range, among entries matching domain when domain != -1, and uses it as the [mem_start, mem_end] window (entry 0 if none matched); otherwise the window is all of memory. It then picks the phys_avail chunk with the largest size among those whose end is not above mem_end and for which end - alloc_size is not below mem_start (chunk 0 if none qualifies; alloc_size is not yet rounded here). alloc_size is then rounded up to a whole page. If it equals PAGE_SIZE the page at the start of the chosen chunk is returned and the chunk's start advances by PAGE_SIZE, without checking that the chunk is non-empty. Otherwise align = (chunk end) & (alloc_size - 1); if alloc_size + align exceeds the chunk size it panics; if align is non-zero the tail of align bytes is split into its own chunk with vm_phys_avail_split, or simply discarded (chunk end reduced by align) when the split fails; then the chunk end is reduced by alloc_size and returned as the address, so the block lies at the end of the chunk. The region returned is removed from phys_avail[]; the caller owns it.
note: reviewer round15 right: the mem_affinity loop ends at the first entry with end - start == 0, not end == 0 (vm_phys.c:1960-1963). Also the single-page path has no size check; the KASSERT on domain is debug-only

name: vm_reserv_reclaim_contig
prose: vm_reserv_reclaim_contig(domain, npages, low, high, alignment, boundary) searches the domain's partially populated reservation queue for the least recently changed reservation that has npages contiguous free pages satisfying the physical address range [low, high) and the alignment and boundary constraints; if one is found the reservation is broken and the first page of that run is returned, otherwise NULL is returned. The slice named vm_reserv_alloc_contig is actually this function (vm_reserv.c:1273-1370); vm_reserv_alloc_contig is a different function. It returns NULL at once if npages > VM_LEVEL_0_NPAGES - 1 or if vm_addr_bound_ok(0, size, boundary) fails. Otherwise it takes the per-domain scan lock and the domain reservation lock and walks the queue: reservations entirely below low, entirely above high or with unaligned start are skipped; for the others it locks the reservation (using a marker entry in the queue while the domain lock is dropped if the trylock fails, and skipping the reservation if the queue changed meanwhile), computes the page window inside the reservation allowed by low and high and calls vm_reserv_find_contig. When a position is found it releases the scan lock, adds npages to popcnt, sets the matching popmap bits, calls vm_reserv_reclaim to break the reservation, releases the reservation lock and returns the page at that position (after a KASSERT that its address satisfies alignment and boundary). If the walk ends without a match it releases the domain lock and the scan lock and returns NULL.
note: reviewer round15 right: the slice shown is vm_reserv_reclaim_contig, not vm_reserv_alloc_contig; the old prose described alloc_contig (vm_reserv.c:688-824), which is a different function. Fixed under the real name of the sliced code

name: vm_reserv_populate
prose: vm_reserv_populate(rv, index) marks page index of reservation rv as populated; rv must be locked, rv->object non-NULL, the popmap bit at index clear, popcnt below VM_LEVEL_0_NPAGES, rv->pages->psind in [0, VM_LEVEL_0_PSIND), and rv->domain valid (KASSERTs, debug builds). It sets the popmap bit, increments popcnt, and, when VM_SUBLEVEL_0_NPAGES is defined and the sublevel containing index is now full, sets psind = 1 on that sublevel's first page. If fewer than PARTPOPSLOP ticks have passed since rv->lasttick, rv is on the partially populated queue and popcnt is not yet VM_LEVEL_0_NPAGES, it returns without touching the queue. Otherwise it sets lasttick to ticks and, under the domain reservation lock, removes rv from the queue if it is on it, then if popcnt < VM_LEVEL_0_NPAGES appends it to the tail and sets inpartpopq, or, when the reservation became full, asserts (KASSERT) that rv->pages->psind == VM_LEVEL_0_PSIND - 1 and sets it to VM_LEVEL_0_PSIND, leaving rv off the queue. It returns void.
note: reviewers right: round15 (psind must be VM_LEVEL_0_PSIND - 1 when full, a KASSERT at vm_reserv.c:664) and round2 (sublevel psind), original (PARTPOPSLOP skip); vm_reserv.c:625-670

name: vnode_pager_setsize
prose: vnode_pager_setsize(vp, nsize) tells the VM system that the file's size changed; it returns void. It returns at once if vp->v_object is NULL. In INVARIANTS builds, if vp->v_mount is non-NULL and the mount does not have MNTK_VMSETSIZE_BUG, it asserts that vp is exclusively locked. It takes the object write lock; if the object is OBJT_DEAD, or nsize already equals the stored vnp_size, it unlocks and returns without changes. Otherwise it computes nobjsize = OFF_TO_IDX(nsize + PAGE_MASK). If the file shrank (nsize < vnp_size) it removes cached pages from nobjsize up to the old object size when nobjsize < object->size, and if nsize is not page-aligned it grabs the page containing nsize without creating it; if that page exists and is not entirely invalid it calls vnode_pager_subpage_purge on the bytes from nsize to the end of the page, and the page is then unbusied. In every case that reaches the end, it stores nsize as vnp_size, sets object->size = nobjsize and unlocks the object. Growth only updates the two sizes.
note: reviewers right: round15 (assertion only when v_mount != NULL), round2 (purge only if page exists and is not none-valid), original (function takes the object lock itself; dead object returns before updating vnp_size); vnode_pager.c:496-563

name: KEntryMap::getEntryOption
prose: KEntryMap::getEntryOption(it, option) const returns one flag of the entry that it refers to, without modifying anything. If it equals cend() it returns false. Otherwise, depending on option, it returns bDirty (EntryDirty), the key's bLocal (EntryLocalized), bGlobal (EntryGlobal), bImmutable (EntryImmutable), bDeleted (EntryDeleted), bExpand (EntryExpansion) or bNotify (EntryNotify), and false for any other option value.
note: slice cut the head; real name KEntryMap::getEntryOption (kconfigdata.cpp:251-275); old prose required a dereferenceable iterator but the end iterator is handled

name: KCoreConfigSkeleton::useDefaults
prose: KCoreConfigSkeleton::useDefaults(b) switches the skeleton between its normal values and default values. If b equals the current mode d->mUseDefaults it returns that mode (that is, b) and changes nothing. Otherwise it stores b in d->mUseDefaults, calls swapDefault() on every item in d->mItems, calls the virtual usrUseDefaults(b), and returns !d->mUseDefaults, which is the previous mode unless usrUseDefaults changed d->mUseDefaults.
note: checked against kcoreconfigskeleton.cpp:1268-1281; prose was correct

name: main
prose: main(argc, argv) of kconfig_compiler generates a configuration class from a .kcfg XML file and a .kcfgc code-generation file. It creates a QCoreApplication and parses the command line (QCommandLineParser::process may itself exit on --help, --version or a parse error). With --license it prints the license text and returns 0. It returns 1 with a message if fewer than two or more than two positional arguments are given. Otherwise it takes the .kcfg and .kcfgc names, ensures the output directory (-d, default '.') ends with a slash, creates the parameter and XML parser objects, parses the XML, and returns 1 if hasErrors(...) reports a problem; otherwise it adds up the non-modify signals, derives baseName by dropping the last five characters of the input file name, runs the header and source generators (start() then save() each), frees the parsed entries and falls off the end of main, which returns 0.

name: KDirWatchPrivate::removeEntry(KDirWatch *instance, const QString &_path, Entry *sub_entry)
prose: KDirWatchPrivate::removeEntry(instance, _path, sub_entry) looks up the entry registered for _path with entry(_path); if there is none it does nothing; otherwise it calls removeEntry(instance, e, sub_entry) on it. That removes sub_entry from the entry's sub-entry list (or, when sub_entry is NULL, removes the client instance from the entry's clients), so the entry is always changed when it exists; it is dropped from the watch (queued in removeList when delayRemove is set, otherwise unwatched, its StatMode counters updated, its inotify mapping removed and erased from m_mapEntries) only if no clients and no sub-entries are left, in which case the entry pointer becomes invalid. instance may be NULL only when sub_entry is non-NULL.
note: reviewer round15 right on the Entry overload prose ('e unchanged' is wrong when the client or sub-entry was already removed); kdirwatch.cpp:959-967

name: KDirWatchPrivate::removeEntry(KDirWatch *instance, Entry *e, Entry *sub_entry)
prose: KDirWatchPrivate::removeEntry(instance, e, sub_entry) first removes e from removeList. It then removes sub_entry from e->m_entries, or, when sub_entry is NULL, removes the client instance from e (the entry is modified before any early return). If e still has clients or sub-entries it returns. Otherwise, if delayRemove is set it inserts e into removeList (e stays in m_mapEntries, now invalid) and returns. Otherwise, if e's status is Normal it calls removeWatch(e); if not (a NonExistent entry) it removes e from its parent entry by calling removeEntry(nullptr, parent path, e), recursively. If e's mode is StatMode it decrements statEntries and stops the stat rescan timer when it reaches 0; it then removes e's inotify watch descriptor mapping and erases e from m_mapEntries, so the pointer e is no longer valid. It returns void.
note: reviewer round15 right ('returns with e unchanged' was false: the client / sub-entry has already been removed at line 973-977); kdirwatch.cpp:969-1017

name: KJob::emitResult
prose: KJob::emitResult() does nothing if the job is already finished. Otherwise it calls finishJob(true), which sets the finished flag, quits the job's event loop if exec() is running one, emits finished(this), then emits result(this), and finally calls deleteLater() if the job is set to auto-delete. Calling it again after that has no further effect.
